newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower, pressured by falls on NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower, pressured by falls on NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent closed lower on Tuesday pressured by sharp falls in NYMEX crude on profit-taking ahead of the expiry of the May crude contract, traders said.
June IPE Brent settled 35 cents lower at $17.99 a barrel, having broken the $18.00 psychological support level in the final ten minutes of trade. The close compared with an intra-day high of $18.64.
Traders said IPE Brent had been pressured lower by losses on NYMEX which saw profit-taking ahead of the May crude contract's expiry at the end of the session.
"People were already a bit sceptical about the higher levels and the NYMEX fall just piled on the selling pressure," said one trader.
On NYMEX, May was trading 88 cents lower at 19.50 a barrel at 1931 GMT, while the June contract was 42 cents down at $19.65 a barrel.
Traders said news of possible delays in Nigerian Bonny crude exports due to a strike by contractors at the tanker terminal had lent the market minimal support earlier on.

As did news that Iraq was pressing on with it plans to ferry by helicopter Moslem pilgrims from its southern border with Saudi Arabia to various Iraqi destinations, despite U.S. warnings against violating a post-Gulf War "no fly zone."

"It's not surprising to see Brent returning to the lower levels of its recent trading range given the market's near neutral response to the Iraqi and Nigeria news," another trader said. "Now it all hinges on what the APIs come up with."

According to a Reuters Survey, analysts expect American Petroleum Institute (API) data out late on Tuesday to show crude stocks grew by 1.0 million barrels, distillate stocks fell 500,000 barrels and gasoline stocks fell 1.3 million barrels in the week ended April 18.

In the week ended April 11, API data showed crude stocks rose 2.973 million barrels, distillates 2.586 million barrels and gasoline 3.627 million barrels. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
